QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_21

question.text: What role does a Professional Clearing Member (PCM) play in the interest rate derivatives market?

answer.text: A PCM has only clearing rights, not trading rights, and clears/settles trades executed by trading members and custodial participants
A PCM trades on its own account and also clears for others
A PCM is a retail participant who clears through a broker
A PCM is a bank that provides clearing bank services to the exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the ETIRD workbook (p.228), a Professional Clearing Member has only clearing rights and no trading rights. A PCM clears and settles trades executed by trading members and custodial participants, without trading on its own account. The Trap: Trading cum Clearing Members both trade and clear — that is a different category. PCMs are not retail participants. Clearing banks are separate entities that facilitate fund transfers. Note: Remember the PCM definition includes both trading members and custodial participants among the entities whose trades it clears and settles.
